description.narrative: On October 10, 2020, the National Assembly Standing Committee on Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development (MOPHRD) unanimously approved the country's first-ever ‘National Emigration Policy'. An action plan to implement the national emigration and welfare policy has also been drafted. The Policy awaits final approval from Federal Cabinet and then its implementation will be started. The policy provides an overarching framework on labour migration and welfare and reintegration of migrant workers. The action plan aims to provide overall guidance to achieve the objectives. Reference to international frameworks including the SGDs and Global Compact on Safe Orderly and Regular Migration are embedded in the policy. The policy also includes specific elements on Fair recruitment in line with ILO General Principles and Operation Guidelines for Fair Recruitment. The ILO, with support of the European Union, has provided technical support to the Government during the policy development process. ILO review to the policy and technical inputs provided guidance on aligning the policy and action plan with relevant ILO instruments and specifically the General Principles and Operational Guidelines for Fair Recruitment. The ILO's inputs were duly acknowledged and incorporated. The draft has been through a series of revisions and consultations among key stakeholders, including social partners. ILO technical support to the policy builds on work commenced in the 2018-19 biennium, when ILO supported consultations, the creation of technical working groups, and technical review of the policy to ensure its alignment with ILS.

description.narrative: Pakistan improved pre-departure orientation with new measures to reduce processing times, simplify procedures and reduce risk of fraud, including: Computerization of registration; illegal job advertisements campaign; Overseas Employment Promoters (OEPs) are bound to mention cost to be incurred; Undertaking regarding cost by individuals proceeding abroad on direct visa; submission by OEPs on the total recruitment at the time of approval; Matching jobs with job seekers data; Uploading of verified foreign jobs on Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment website; awareness campaign through print, electronic & social media; regulatory measures against Test Trade centres; and comprehensive complaint mechanism system. The National Vocational & Technical Training Commission established ten training and resource facilitation centres, which provide services to intending migrant workers: soft skills, language, laws and working environment, technical skills, recognition of prior learning, training and skills testing; attestation and verification of TVET certification; coordination with OEPs, Trade Testing Centres (TTCs) and National Employment Exchange (NEX) The Pakistan Workers Federation has established thirty Resource Centres where potential migrant workers can receive pre-departure orientation. between July 2020-June 2021 24,000 individuals visited the centres. Information, education and communication materials have been developed, including COVID-19 relevant information (in Urdu). Community and trade union information sessions reached 4,500 migrant workers and trade union members. The Italian Trade Union Centre is providing new information service for Pakistani diaspora to access decent work in Italy, Pakistani investment opportunities, knowledge-sharing and joint ventures. Services include: Italian translation of Labour Laws and awareness raising; regional Pakistani diaspore focal points identified; face-to-face training, and new web-page with fact sheets With the support of the European Union (EU), Government Protectorate Officers were trained on improved communication techniques and adopting improved ‘Pre-Departure Orientation Training (PDOT). The ILO, with assistance of the EU, supported the Pakistan Workers Federation (PWF) by training, development of materials, awareness-raising, and support to the setup of Resource Centres at 30 PWF District Offices. Booklets disseminated through PWF website, face book page, whats App groups and the indirect beneficiaries reached to over 150,000 persons through digital means and word of mouth. The ILO made a substantial contribution in outreach to migrant workers through the establishment of the "community-based change-makers programme" (involving 5 CSOs and 27 change-makers), which has reached more than 9,800 women and men intending migrant workers. The program entailed close engagement with relevant public administrations in the selected districts to ensure institutional capacity building and sustainability. In addition, the ILO has provided capacity building to the Pakistan Workers Federation and its eight regional offices through an intensive training of trainers program. A pool of 35 trainers rolled out awareness raising sessions at constituency level and educated 2,600 women and men on fair recruitment and safe and regular migration channels and procedures. With the support of the EU, ILO supported National Vocational & Technical Training Commission (NAVTTC) in conceptualizing the ‘Country of Destination specific Facilitation & Resource Centres' for migrant workers and its operationalization. 10 Officials from NAVTTC Facilitation Centres participated in ILO training course on ‘Pre-Departure Orientation Training. ILO, with assistance from the Government of Italy, is working with Pakistani diaspora in Italy through its Implementing Partner, Italian Trade Union Centre (ISCOS), to raise awareness among Pakistani workers and engaging Pakistani-origin businesspersons.
